Definition: probably from G4078 (through the idea of gushing plumply); a fount (literally or figuratively), i.e. source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment) (not necessarily the original spring):--fountain, well.
BiblicalUsage: A pege is a spring, a fountain of water. Jesus told the Samaritan woman that the water He gives becomes a well springing up into everlasting life, and James asks whether one fountain can send out sweet water and bitter. In Revelation the Lamb leads His people to living fountains of waters, and God gives the fountain of the water of life freely to him that is athirst.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that the fountain is the picture of grace itself: it does not run dry, it is not earned, and it is given freely to the thirsty. I will not draw from a bitter spring when the living fountain is open, and I will not keep it to myself when others are thirsty. The Lamb leads to the water — that is the whole gospel in one image.
